title: caltha palustris var. typica
intro: Caltha palustris var. typica, commonly known as Marsh Marigold, is a flowering plant that belongs to the Ranunculaceae family. It has been traditionally used for its medicinal properties, which include providing relief from inflammation, fever, and respiratory issues, such as bronchitis and coughs. The therapeutic actions of Marsh Marigold include expectorant, anti-inflammatory, and antiseptic properties, which are attributed to its bioactive constituents, including alkaloids, flavonoids, and glycosides. These constituents also contribute to the plant's ability to stimulate digestion, treat skin conditions, and exhibit antioxidant and antimicrobial activities.
